ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence screening of all shareholders, directors, legal representatives, and ultimate beneficial owners against: (i) Colombian Office of the Attorney General and UIAF lists; (ii) OFAC SDN List and sectoral sanctions; (iii) UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; (iv) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (v) Interpol red notices and related alerts; (vi) PEP databases maintained by international financial intelligence units and commercial vendors; and (vii) Colombian national extortion and terrorism financing lists (Listas de Medidas Preventivas). Where a PEP or nexus to a sanctioned jurisdiction is identified, the appointing compliance officer must file a suspicious transaction report (ROS) with the UIAF, obtain senior management approval, and may reject incorporation if verification cannot be completed.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) and the official online portal of the Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá / Superintendencia de Sociedades (Cámara de Comercio electronic name reservation system, 'Sistema de Información Registral' operated by Confecámaras)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name may be registered in Spanish or in a foreign language provided that it is expressed in Latin script and is pronounceable in accordance with Spanish phonetic rules; the name must be distinguishable from existing registered names in the same registry; transliteration of non-Latin script names must be certified by a sworn translator (traductor oficial) recognized by the Colombian Ministry of Foreign Affairs; the registered name must include the suffix 'S.A.S.' (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada) and may not mislead the public as to its corporate purpose or legal form.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banco, Bancolombia, Financiera, Fondo de Inversión, Bolsa, Valores (requires prior express authorization from the Financial Superintendency of Colombia)
Aseguradora, Seguros, Reaseguros (requires prior authorization from the Financial Superintendency of Colombia)
Colombia, Nacional, Presidencia, Ministerio, Superintendencia, DIAN, Gobierno, Banco de la República (requires authorization from the relevant government entity or constitutes misrepresentation)
URBE, Zona Franca (requires prior authorization from the national planning authority or special regime entity)
Cooperativa, Mutual, Previsión (requires prior authorization from the Superintendencia de Economía Solidaria)
Petróleo, Minera, Hidrocarburos, Energía (may require prior ministerial concession or regulatory approval)
Operador Turístico, Agencia de Viajes (requires prior authorization from the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Tourism in specific regulated cases)
Restaurante, Hotpot (allowed but subject to sanitary trademark and commercial registry utility checks; may be restricted if identical or confusingly similar to a registered trademark or trade name)
Alcohol, Licores, Cerveza, Tabaco (requires prior sanitary and possibly tax authorization)
Farmacéutica, Droguería, Salud (requires prior INVIMA authorization)
Keywords implying public utility, defense, aviation, telecommunications, or broadcasting (require specific sector regulator authorization)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant may submit a written reconsideration request to the same Chamber of Commerce registry official within ten (10) business days of the rejection notice, stating the legal grounds of distinctiveness. If the Chamber of Commerce maintains the rejection, the applicant may file an administrative appeal (recurso de reposición y en subsidio apelación) before the Superintendencia de Sociedades through the e-government portal (Servicios Ciudadano Digital) within five (5) business days. The appeal must attach a copy of the rejection decision, a comparative list of existing registered names, and evidence of trademark or trade name availability from the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC). The Superintendencia de Sociedades must resolve the appeal within thirty (30) business days. A new name reservation request may be filed simultaneously to avoid expiry of the underlying business project timelines.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only for preliminary registration purposes if a physical address is designated and a local agent (representante legal) is appointed; however, for a full-service dining chain (ISIC 5610) with target payment rails through local merchant acquiring and POS, the Chamber of Commerce and municipal authorities require an actual operational premises that satisfies sanitary, zoning, fire-safety, and municipal commercial license requirements. A virtual office may not be used to obtain the mandatory sanitary registration (Registro Sanitario) or operating permit issued by the municipal mayor's office or the District Health Secretariat. The virtual office arrangement is therefore assessed as permissible for receipt of corporate correspondence but not as a substitute for the required commercial establishment.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High likelihood (75-85%) for a restaurant business within the first 12 months of operation due to mandatory sanitary inspections by the Secretaría Distrital de Salud, municipal zoning and noise inspections, fire department inspections, and consumer protection verification visits by the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio. Unannounced inspections are common in the food and beverage sector.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per Superintendencia de Sociedades resolution (approx. 0.0016 UVT set by annual decree)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial registry fee and certificate of existence and legal representation (Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per 2024 official registry fee schedule

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada), Código de Comercio (Decreto 410 de 1971), arts. 52-60, 98-110; Decreto Único Reglamentario 1074 de 2015 (RUES); Ley 1429 de 2010 (formalización empresarial); Ley 1801 de 2016 (Código Nacional de Policía, registro de actividad comercial); Resolución 2674 de 2013 (requisitos sanitarios para servicios de alimentos)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá (or local Chamber of Commerce) through the Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) single window
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private incorporation instrument) executed by all shareholders and filed electronically or in person with the Chamber of Commerce; optional notarial authentication required only if real property is contributed
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for a Colombian S.A.S. under Ley 1258/2008; the by-laws may freely set the authorized capital, and paid-in capital may be zero at incorporation. Cash contributions may be deferred for up to 24 months; no escrow account or bank deposit certificate is a precondition for registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION. FIRST: The share subscriptions recorded in the incorporation instrument are ratified. SECOND: The registered office is fixed at [address], Bogotá, Colombia, as principal place of business for all legal, tax, and judicial notices. THIRD: [Name] is appointed General Manager and legal representative, and [Name] is appointed Treasurer, each authorized to open bank accounts and sign supplier and employee contracts. FOURTH: The General Manager is authorized to register the Company before the Cámara de Comercio, to obtain the NIT/RUT with DIAN, and to secure every sanitary, environmental, fire, and municipal license required for the operation of the hotpot restaurant. FIFTH: All prior acts performed on behalf of the Company are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-validation of Corporate Name (Certificado de Homonimia)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá – RUES digital portal (www.rues.org.co)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the RUES portal and submit up to three proposed corporate names in order of preference. The system scans the Chamber of Commerce database and issues a certificate of homonyms confirming whether the requested denomination is available for an S.A.S. The certificate is valid for 60 calendar days.
required_dossiers: Completed online RUES form
Shareholder identification documents or passports
List of up to three proposed corporate names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file alternative names immediately in the same session, or lodge a recurso de reposición with the Chamber registry officer within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Private Incorporation Instrument
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founders' private act (authentication before a Notary Public only if real estate is contributed or at shareholders' election)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Documento Privado de Constitución in Spanish containing: (a) shareholder identification; (b) S.A.S. status declaration; (c) capital subscription schedule; (d) share classes and voting rights; (e) corporate duration; (f) management bodies; (g) dispute resolution rules. All shareholders sign every page; signatures are notarized where real property is contributed.
required_dossiers: Draft incorporation instrument and by-laws
Valid identification documents of each shareholder and legal representative
Certificate of homonyms from Step 1
RUT pre-assignment from DIAN if already obtained
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Defective clauses are cured by executing an amendment (reforma) or re-executing the instrument before the same notarial or private act prior to filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Chamber of Commerce (RUES)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá / Ventanilla Única Empresarial (RUES)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation instrument and RUES forms online or in person at the Chamber. Pay the registration tariff and the impuesto de registro (registry tax, approximately 0.7% of subscribed capital in Bogotá). Upon approval the Chamber issues the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal within the SLA and transmits registration data electronically to DIAN for automatic NIT assignment.
required_dossiers: Signed incorporation instrument
Certificate of homonyms
Formulario Registro Único Empresarial
Proof of registered office address (lease agreement or title deed)
Copies of shareholder and legal representative identification documents
Proof of payment of registry fees and taxes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The Chamber issues an oficio de subsanación listing deficiencies; the applicant has 60 calendar days to correct and refile. After the deadline a new application and fee are required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration - NIT and RUT with DIAN
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales) – online RUT module
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the provisional NIT generated upon Chamber registration, complete the RUT electronic form, and record the legal representative, tax regime, VAT responsibilities for restaurant services, ICA obligations, and invoicing requirements. The RUT is delivered electronically as a QR-verified PDF.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
National ID (cédula) or passport of the legal representative
Company email and Colombian contact details
Beneficial owner information for non-resident shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request a correction of the RUT through the DIAN portal or regional administration office; corrective updates generally become effective within 24 hours.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration and Sealing of Statutory Books
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá (Registro de Libros de Comercio)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the statutory books (shareholder register, board minutes book, assembly minutes book, capital contributions register) for numbering, sealing, and registration at the Chamber in accordance with Código de Comercio articles 52-60.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Physical or digital set of statutory books
Payment receipt of the book stamping fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Re-apply with a new set of books if the previous set cannot be sealed due to binding or formatting defects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Corporate Bank Account and Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank with merchant acquiring and POS capability (e.g., Bancolombia, Davivienda, BBVA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate checking account, deposit any paid-in capital, and obtain a certificate of deposit. Simultaneously request a merchant account and POS terminals for future restaurant payment rails.
required_dossiers: NIT and RUT
Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Board resolution appointing the legal representative
Passport copies and beneficial ownership declaration of all shareholders
Utility bill evidencing business address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Supplement any missing KYC or AML documentation requested by the bank's compliance unit; resubmit within 10 business days to avoid account closure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Zoning Verification and Commercial Activity Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alcaldía Local / Subsecretaría de Control Urbanístico – Ventanilla Única de Registro de Actividad (Ley 1801 de 2016)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify that the premises' land-use classification permits full-service dining (ISIC 5610), obtain the Certificado de Uso de Suelo, and complete the Registro Único de Actividad through the municipal one-stop shop. This registration consolidates police-law compliance and validates the operating address.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Lease or ownership instrument for the premises
RUT evidencing payment and registration of ICA (industry and commerce tax)
Preliminary sanitary concept for the food-service operation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File an urbanistic pre-consultation (consulta de uso de suelo) with the local planning authority; if the zoning is incompatible, select alternative commercial premises and re-register.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Secretaría Distrital de Salud (Bogotá) or municipal health authority; Secretaría Distrital de Ambiente (Bogotá) or Corporación Autónoma Regional (CAR) for other municipalities; Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos; Alcaldía Local under Ley 1801 de 2016
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Certificado de Concepto Sanitario (Resolución 2674/2013), Registro Único de Actividad (Ley 1801/2016) and simplified Plan de Manejo Ambiental

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Secretaría Distrital de Ambiente (Bogotá) or the Corporación Autónoma Regional with jurisdiction over the restaurant municipality
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category III – Simplified Environmental Compliance Registration (Plan de Manejo Ambiental simplificado); full Environmental Impact Assessment study is not required for a single food-service establishment under Decreto 1076/2015, Art. 2.2.2.3.2.2.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges to the municipal sewer must meet Resolución 0631/2015 limits: pH 6.0–9.0, BOD5 ≤ 500 mg/L, TSS ≤ 500 mg/L, COD ≤ 750 mg/L, fats and oils ≤ 100 mg/L (stricter local limits apply in Bogotá per Resolution 3957/2009); mandatory grease trap and oil-water separator; kitchen exhaust and odor control to prevent nuisance; acoustic compliance with Resolución 0627/2006 (commercial zones: 65 dB day / 55 dB night); solid waste separation, storage, and municipal collection per Decreto 2981/2013.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance (Certificado de Bomberos) requiring an approved kitchen range-hood suppression system, ABC extinguishers, emergency exit signage, and evacuation plan; structural and occupancy-load verification through the municipal Uso de Suelo certificate; mandatory Sistema de Gestión de Seguridad y Salud en el Trabajo (SGSST) registration per Decreto 1072/2015 and Resolución 0312/2019.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN); official electronic portal: MUISCA (muisca.dian.gov.co) with institutional site www.dian.gov.co; e-invoicing validation platform: facturaelectronica.dian.gov.co
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Colombian S.A.S. obtains its NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) automatically upon notarized incorporation and Chamber of Commerce registration. The foreign shareholders must appoint a Colombian legal representative with a notarized power of attorney, who then completes the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) enrollment with DIAN, declares the economic activities (CIIU 5610 for restaurant services together with condiment ISIC 1075/4790 as appropriate), selects the IVA responsibility regime, and registers each local establishment. A non-resident enterprise without a Colombian entity must first obtain a NIT through a Colombian agent; however, for this overseas hotpot direct-operated chain the operating arm is the resident CO_SAS, which must register before issuing any invoice. Statutory licenses from municipality and sanitary authority must precede the DIAN RUT finalization.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; the S.A.S. is a resident juridical person subject to corporate income tax (CIT) on worldwide income at 30% for tax years beginning 2025 (35% for tax years 2023-2024 under Law 2277/2022). Colombia does not recognize US-style check-the-box pass-through for a domestic SAS; the entity itself is the taxpayer. The source-based territorial rules apply only to non-residents and permanent establishments, while the Colombian SAS must include both Colombian-source and foreign-source income with a foreign tax credit. A 9% preferential CIT rate may apply to certain newly created companies in agro-industrial or creative export activities under Law 1429/2010 and Law 1955/2019 conditions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists in Colombia. Available statutory mechanisms include: (a) the SIMPLE regime (Régimen Simple de Tributación), an optional consolidated substitution tax covering income tax, VAT and municipal taxes for eligible small businesses below the UVT-indexed threshold under Law 1943/2018; (b) election of the 9% preferential CIT regime for qualifying new export-oriented creative/agro-industrial companies subject to minimum employment and net-worth conditions; (c) application of free-trade-zone (Zona Franca) treatment at 20% CIT with prior DIAN authorization; (d) advanced pricing agreements and mutual agreement procedures for transfer pricing; and (e) mandatory anti-hybrid neutrality rules disqualifying deduction of hybrid mismatch payments under Law 2277/2022.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold for full VAT-registered responsibility: every person selling taxable goods or rendering taxable services in Colombia must register in the RUT as Responsable de IVA. Persons whose gross income in the prior calendar year is below 3,500 UVT (approximately COP 154,000,000 in 2024) may be treated as 'No Responsables', but this exception does not exempt a hotpot restaurant because on-premise meal service and beverage sales are expressly taxable activities; thus the CO_SAS must obtain IVA responsibility status from inception. Businesses under the SIMPLE regime are also considered VAT registrants for invoicing purposes. Exporters remain registered even if their export-only turnover would otherwise fall below the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All Colombian taxpayers, including restaurant operators, must issue electronic sales invoices (Factura Electrónica de Venta) using DIAN-authorized software or the free DIAN app. Each invoice is transmitted in real time to DIAN's web service using a digital certificate; DIAN validates the XML, assigns a unique electronic invoicing code (CUFE/CUDS), and returns the authorization status before the invoice may be delivered to the customer. The restaurant POS must sync directly into the e-invoicing engine, and each emitted invoice must include the mandatory QR code. No paper stamp or physical pre-printed invoice may be used. Export invoices require a specific 'export status' annotation to obtain zero-rated or excluded treatment, and customs clearance is cross-matched electronicaly with DIAN's SIGO and VUCE platforms.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Colombian VAT territoriality rule, exports of goods are excluded from VAT but confer the exporter the right to recover input VAT (exporters' VAT refund mechanism). The CO_SAS may zero-rate: (i) physical exports of hotpot condiments, sauces, packaged meal kits and related tangibles, evidenced by customs export declarations; (ii) offshore services, franchise management, know-how, software and BPO services rendered to an overseas franchisee or related foreign entity, provided the beneficiary is tax-resident abroad, the service is wholly used and economically consumed outside Colombia, and the contract and invoicing clearly identify the foreign user; and (iii) servicing of overseas direct-operated restaurants where the consideration is paid in foreign currency and no taxable activity occurs in Colombian territory. Goods and services sold to local Colombian customers are taxable at the general 19% rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Customs Declaration (Declaración de Exportación - DEX), filed electronically through SIGO/VUCE and validated by DIAN customs authorities
Bill of Lading for maritime shipments or Air Waybill for air cargo, evidencing physical departure of the goods from Colombian customs territory

Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Cambio y Liquidación de Divisas) issued by the local intermediary bank confirming that the export proceeds have been repatriated and sold in the Colombian foreign exchange market
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN reconciles the DEX, the electronic export invoice status, customs exit records and the foreign-exchange certificate; failure to remit export proceeds within the statutory 180-day term or absence of admissible transport documents triggers automatic reversal of the zero-rating. DIAN assesses the omitted IVA at 19% plus daily default interest and imposes a penalty of up to 100% of the tax omitted under Estatuto Tributario Article 648; fraudulent invoicing, fake export declarations or misused export refunds expose the SAS to criminal liability for tax evasion under Law 2277/2022, retroactivity up to the 5-year limitation period, disqualification from the 9% export incentive regime, and joint personal liability of the legal representative and tax preparer.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (Bank of the Republic of Colombia), Colombia's central bank, is the constitutional authority for the administration of foreign exchange control. It regulates the official foreign exchange market through the Circular Reglamentaria DCIN-83, computes the official TRM (Tasa Representativa del Mercado), maintains the Foreign Investment Registry, authorizes foreign exchange intermediaries (intermediarios del mercado cambiario), and issues the exchange-control sanctions framework under Ley 9 de 1991, together with the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia which supervises banks and enforces AML/KYC obligations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Renewal of the Commercial Registry (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil) with update of the Single Business Registry (RUES) data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio (Chamber of Commerce) of the registered domicile jurisdiction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March covering the immediately preceding calendar year; uniform statutory deadline for all merchants, no extension available
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers the monetary fine set by Article 87 of the Commercial Code plus exclusion from preferential state benefits; a company failing to renew is marked as non-renovant in the RUES, and after repeated non-renewal and the Chamber of Commerce administrative procedure, the commercial registration is cancelled, extinguishing the company's legal capacity and forcing dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Prior-Year Financial Statements approved by the Shareholders' Meeting and filed with the Chamber of Commerce (Estados Financieros de Propósito General)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio (and Superintendencia de Sociedades for supervised entities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' Assembly must approve the accounts within three months of fiscal-year close (by 31 March); approved statements must be registered with the Chamber of Commerce within the Chamber's published filing window (typically running from early April through 30 June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unregistered financial statements are unenforceable against third parties and prevent lawful dividend distribution; the Chamber of Commerce may impose its tariffed filing fine; the Superintendencia de Sociedades may order corrective compliance under Law 222 of 1995 for continuing non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios) including mandatory declaration of foreign-held assets and controlled-foreign-company information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between 15 April and 6 June of the following fiscal year, staggered by the last two digits of the NIT per the DIAN calendar resolution (for FY2024: 15 April to 6 June 2025)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% per month on tax payable capped at 100% plus default interest (Articles 634 and 641 E.T.); non-filing permits official estimation by DIAN, administrative seizure, and criminal liability for fraudulent tax evasion under Article 402 E.T.; persistent non-filing enables banking and export embargoes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Exogenous Information Report (Información Exógena Tributaria) covering transactions with third parties
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, typically by early May following the tax period (for FY2024: 9 May 2025 per DIAN Resolution 000029), staggered by the last two digits of the NIT; no grace period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure or untimely delivery is sanctioned under Article 651 E.T. with fines up to 15,000 UVT (approximately COP 705.9 million / USD 174,000 for 2025), reducible to 15% of the base sanction for voluntary late filing; inaccurate reports are treated as non-filed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal Industry and Commerce Tax (Impuesto de Industria y Comercio - ICA) Annual Return and prior-year reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Municipal Treasury (Secretaría de Hacienda or equivalent local tax authority of the municipality where the restaurant establishment operates)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within four months following fiscal-year end, exact date per municipal tax calendar (e.g., Bogotá simplified regime: 31 January; general regime: bimonthly accruals with annual reconciliation); overseas revenues are outside the municipal territorial tax base
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts the municipal fine foreseen in the Código de Rentas (up to 100% of the tax due) plus arrears interest; continued default authorizes embargo of bank accounts and property and suspension or revocation of the local commercial operating license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of the Single Registry of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales - RUB)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually per DIAN Resolution, staggered by the last two digits of the NIT with the filing window normally published for the second calendar quarter (FY2024 cycle filed during 2025)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to identify and update the ultimate beneficial owner exposes the entity to sanctions under Article 651 E.T. (up to 15,000 UVT), plus impediments to obtaining tax clearance certificates and participating in public procurement.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory auditor (revisor fiscal) where gross assets or gross ordinary income at the prior year-end exceed 5,000 current monthly minimum wages (SMMLV 2025: approximately COP 7.1175 billion / USD 1.75 million) or workforce exceeds 200 employees (Articles 203-205 of the Commercial Code, as applied to S.A.S. entities under Article 29 of Law 1258 of 2008). An independent certified audit is not mandatory below these thresholds, but shareholders may voluntarily appoint a revisor fiscal, or a third party such as a bank, franchisor, or investor may contract a certified audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Colombian GAAP under Law 1314 of 2009 adopting IFRS (NIIF): Grupo 1 - full IFRS; Grupo 2 - IFRS for SMEs (NIIF para PYMES), most commonly applied by a mid-size restaurant S.A.S.; Grupo 3 - local simplified micro-entity framework. Financial statements must be prepared by a registered public accountant (contador público) and, where the thresholds are met, audited by a certified statutory auditor (revisor fiscal).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At least once per year, the S.A.S. must remit the RUB report to DIAN identifying every ultimate beneficial owner holding, directly or indirectly, 10% or more of the capital, voting rights, or economic benefit, or exercising control, including non-resident owners permitted under the S.A.S. regime. All share transfers and capital movements occurring during the completed fiscal year must be reflected in the report even in the absence of ownership changes. The annual confirmation is due in the DIAN calendar staggered by NIT digits and must be re-filed on a sworn basis that the prior data remains current.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro de Registro de Accionistas) recording each shareholder and all share transfers
Register of Directors (Libro de Actas de Junta Directiva) recording resolutions of the management body
Minute Book (Libro de Actas de Asamblea de Accionistas) recording shareholders' meeting minutes and profit distribution agreements

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300-1,200 (annual registered office or commercial compliance agent fee; Bogotá, Medellín and Cali market range for S.A.S. representation services)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500-8,000 (annual certified audit or revisor fiscal engagement for an independently operating mid-size restaurant entity; scope depends on number of establishments and consolidation of overseas restaurant operations)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday is available for full-service dining. The effective rate equals the 35% statutory headline rate after ordinary deductions. General incentives include the additional deduction under Article 158-3 of the Colombian Tax Code (ET) equal to 30% of the cost of new productive fixed assets, and a 50% VAT credit on certain imported capital goods. The 'Orange Economy' preferential rate does not apply to restaurant operations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 110 (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios para Personas Jurídicas) filed through the DIAN electronic portal (MUISCA using 'en banc' or 'declaraciones' service).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due date is set by DIAN Resolution on a staggered schedule based on the last two digits of the NIT. For the fiscal year ending 31 December, the deadline generally falls between 8 April and 12 May of the following calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross operating income from the directly-operated hotpot restaurant, including food and beverage sales and all ancillary condiment and packaged product revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the local SAS's global taxable income; do not segregate the overseas shareholding. The local statutory representative must ensure that all cash and card sales through local acquiring/POS rails are recognised.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-taxable income, exempt income, and capital gains received from third parties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Leave box at zero unless the SAS can support a Colombian exemption or non-taxable character. A non-resident shareholder cannot claim any foreign income exemption on this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ordinary cost of sales and deductions legally authorised, including raw material procurement, salaries, rents, utilities, depreciation, depreciation of POS equipment, and amortisation of restaurant leasehold improvements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border payments for hotpot seasoning and kitchen supplies supplied by related parties must be supported with transfer pricing documentation and must not exceed arm's length value.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions for royalties, interest, and technical services paid to foreign affiliates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare only payments that comply with the beneficial ownership and economic substance requirements; withhold the applicable withholding tax on each category at the statutory or DTA rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable net income before losses: gross income less allowable deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the tax loss carryforward of up to five years under domestic law; calculate limits on the annual offset according to Section 147 ET.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable corporate income tax at 35% on the liquid base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The final computed tax is a liability of the local SAS. Foreign ownership by a non-resident does not change the rate and the local entity must settle the amount in Colombian pesos.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prepayments (anticipos), two-month self-assessed withholdings, and available credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not credit foreign taxes paid by the foreign shareholder; only the SAS's own Colombian prepayments and domestic creditable withholdings are allowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable or balance in favour; the SAS must pay the net balance using the DIAN's electronic bank collection channels.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any balance in favour may be claimed for compensation against next year's anticipo or refunded after a DIAN audit, but no remittance abroad of a refund is allowed without renewal of the foreign shareholder's NIF.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without prior invitation results in a surcharge of 5% of the tax due per month or fraction, capped at 100%, plus a minimum fine of COP 594,000 for 2024. A false declaration attracts a penalty of 35% of the sum under-declared under Article 671 ET, plus default interest and a potential criminal conviction.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a DTA-restrained rate, the non-resident receiving entity must provide the local withholding agent with a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the competent authority of the DTA country, together with a beneficial ownership statement and, for certain treaties, a shareholding qualification certificate. No advance approval from DIAN is required; the withholding agent must keep the TRC in its files for at least five years and must file the informative tax return on foreign payments via Formulario 110 and Schedule 30/31 disclosures.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on cross-border royalties 20%; statutory withholding on foreign interest 15%. Treaty rates typically range between 0% and 15% for interest and 5% and 20% for royalties, depending on the DTA, recipient's nature, and beneficial ownership.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: COP 6,353,775,000 (135,000 UVT for the 2024 taxable year)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia has not enacted a standalone Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) as seen in Caribbean jurisdictions. However, the DIAN applies the doctrine of substance through the general anti-abuse rule in Article 120 ET, the restriction on fictitious transactions, and the requirement of a valid business purpose under Article 658 ET. A foreign-owned local hotpot chain must demonstrate operational substance—employees, managerial oversight, physical restaurant premises, accounting records, and commercial-trading control—before claiming treaty benefits or counterpart documentation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Recording only card transactions on the POS terminal while omitting a substantial portion of cash sales from line 1a of Formulario 110, artificially lowering the taxable base and VAT settlement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 671 ET, an omission entailing underdeclared income attracts a fine of up to 200% of the evaded tax, plus default interest and criminal exposure under Articles 330-332 of the Criminal Code; direct criminal consequence for the local statutory representative.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Legal representatives and sole shareholders of a SAS may face personal civil liability for all unpaid corporate taxes and fines; criminal conviction can result in imprisonment of four to nine years, travel bans, and extradition proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Importing hotpot condiment and custom stove parts from an overseas related supplier at a price materially above arm's length, and failing to prepare or file the local and master file documentation when the turnover threshold is met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN is authorised to increase the SAS's taxable income to the arm's length price; Article 260-11 ET imposes penalties of 1% to 5% of the value of each unreported related-party transaction, plus a specific fine of COP 1,380,000 for each omitted local file and interest on the primary adjustment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The statutory agent is personally liable for the accuracy of transfer pricing declarations; knowingly submitting false certificates constitutes procedural fraud under Article 434 of the Criminal Code, carrying imprisonment of twenty-four to sixty months and disqualification from holding board positions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a zero-substance foreign intermediary to receive parking royalties and trademark royalties from the Colombian restaurant while the actual management and value-creating functions remain in Colombia; the payments are deducted without economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN disallows the entire deduction under the GAAR and Article 120 ET, recharacterises the transaction as fraudulent, applies a 35% penalty on the corrected tax, and imposes the interest accruing from the original due date; if the structure triggers a treaty benefit denial, the entire foreign income remains taxable in Colombia and the foreign intermediary becomes liable for the withheld tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate veil protection is removed under Law 222 of 1995 when the entity is used as a mere instrument to evade taxes; directors and shareholders become jointly and severally liable for all national taxes, interest, and sanctions, and can be barred from leaving Colombia pending resolution of the offence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring cash receipts from hotpot customers to avoid the transaction reporting threshold, using the undocumented cash to pay wages of undeclared staff, and creating an artificial discrepancy between POS data and gross revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 526 of 2021 and the National Code of Compliance, a merchant accepting cash must report cash transactions above COP 12,900,000 (2024) on the Formación SARLAFT; failure to file or structuring transactions constitutes an administrative penalty of up to 5,000 SMLV or suspension of the commercial registration and revocation of the operating license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative is criminally liable for money-laundering under Articles 323-333 of the Criminal Code; if the restaurant is held as a legal fiction to channel illicit capital, directors may be personally fined an amount equal to 150% of the laundered source, receive a travel ban and asset freezing, and serve a prison term of ten to twenty years.
